content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). Alternatively, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. If you are undergoing long-term treatment with this medication, it is essential to have regular laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney function assessments and complete blood counts, to monitor your health. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication in the refrigerator. Discard any unused portion after 14 days, as the drug loses its potency beyond this period. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. It is important to note that this information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Before taking penicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other penicillin-type antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, ampicillin), cephalosporins (e.g., cephalexin, cefuroxime), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, penicillin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may also interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as specific diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. For any questions or concerns about this medication, always consult your healthcare provider for detailed and personalized guidance.
